checks: Fiberwise Hausdorff convergence and finite P give one ball containing every original and perturbed fiber. Exterior points are eventually excluded. If an r-ball about an interior point is contained in K_z, support values for the perturbed fiber in every unit direction differ by at most its Hausdorff distance. When that distance is below r, separation puts the point in the perturbed fiber.

Contracting K_z by any factor strictly below one about an interior point gives a subset of the interior, and its volume tends to full volume. The boundary is therefore volume-null. Dominated convergence of the indicators off that boundary gives convergence of the sum of symmetric-difference volumes Δ_j, with no common affine-centroid requirement.

At a fixed ambient mark each cap and total mass change by at most Δ_j. The same uniform bound compares the two infima over all containing caps. The limit total mass is positive because P is nonempty with positive limit fiber volumes.

Move only the continuous coordinate at p and pair through-mark caps by normal. Pure-base normals leave all sections fixed, even when a section lies on the boundary. Otherwise normalize the continuous coefficient to unit length, so every section cutoff changes by at most the Euclidean mark displacement independently of any base tilt. Cross sections of the common ball have (d−1)-volume at most κ_{d−1}R^{d−1}, which includes d=1 as the interval-length estimate. Integrating across the slab and summing gives the stated coefficient |P|κ_{d−1}R^{d−1}.

The bound is valid for all approaching feasible marks, including a boundary limit mark. Hausdorff convergence provides such marks at p. Division by the convergent positive total gives normalized convergence. In the finite product Hausdorff metric with the mark distance, the sequential estimate gives a single local neighborhood in which a specified strict gap persists for every feasible nearby mark at p.

overlap.comparison: Uses a uniform slab estimate for moving a fixed-base mark with the original body fixed, in a near-active-cap theorem. The present lemma also varies all fibers and tracks the normalized value.

Uses a fixed-body mark displacement estimate in a lattice centerpoint fiber. Its fiber geometry and measure are fixed, whereas the present bound includes the symmetric-difference term for perturbing them.
Gives the through-mark formula and upper semicontinuity/attainment for a fixed actual body. It does not compare two fiber families or give two-sided marked convergence.

Its proof gives fixed-mark total variation comparison and Hausdorff-to-total-variation continuity for ordinary convex bodies in a normalized class. The present statement adds the general fixed finite base and a uniform moving-mark comparison even when vertical caps carry boundary mass.

readability: The depth comparison uses the same normal at each of the two marks, with a separate fixed-location comparison of the two measures. This order avoids assuming joint continuity of cap mass at a vertical normal.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The proof gives convergence at every feasible sequence of marks approaching the given mark at a fixed base. The bound is uniform over all cap normals and preserves any strict normalized gap.
